# Case 1A – Insurance Campaign Response Analysis

Explores the campaign dataset (`dsc_test_case.csv`, 215,993 offers, 3-class outcome: Reject / PA / Life),
builds an interactive dashboard, and trains a propensity model to show how the next campaign could be targeted.

**Deliverables** (all generated by one run, so the numbers always match):
| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `output/Answer Case 1A.html` / `.pdf` | Interactive dashboard / print version |
| `output/Case 1A Presentation.pdf` | 15-slide 16:9 deck for presenting |
| `output/Case 1A Presenter Guide.pdf` | Slide-by-slide guide: how to read each chart, script, key numbers, Q&A, glossary |

## Quick start
```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py            # full run: analysis + model + HTML + PDF  (~10 s)
python main.py --no-pdf   # skip the PDF export
python -m pytest -q       # unit tests
```
The PDF export uses a headless Chromium browser (Microsoft Edge or Chrome) if one is installed.

## Design
Each class has one responsibility, and the pipeline wires them together:

```
CampaignDataLoader ─► DataQualityChecker ─► DataCleaner ─► FeatureEngineer ─► ResponseAnalyzer ─┐
                                                                         └──► PropensityModel ──┤
                                                          HtmlBuilder ◄─────────────────────────┘ ─► PdfExporter
```
- **Configuration is data.** Bins, mappings and thresholds live in `AnalysisConfig`, so nothing is hard-coded in the logic.
- **Typed results.** `DataQualityReport` and `ModelReport` are dataclasses serialised into the dashboard payload.
- **Self-contained output.** `HtmlBuilder` inlines the CSS, the JS and the JSON into a single HTML file with no external dependencies, so it works offline.
- **Front end is also object-oriented.** It has a `Chart` base class with `StackedBarChart`, `LineChart`, `HeatmapChart`, `BubbleChart`, `DivergingBarChart`, `DotRangeChart`, `ColumnChart` and `HBarChart`, plus a `Dashboard` controller for the segment filter.

## Dashboard contents
| Section | Charts |
|---|---|
| KPIs | Acceptance rate (with monthly sparkline), volume, PA, Life, product mix |
| 1 · Campaign performance | Volume columns, acceptance-rate trend lines (Total / PA / Life) |
| 2 · Where the buyers are | Age × income heatmap, age × segment opportunity bubble matrix |
| 3 · What drives acceptance | Diverging response-index chart, age distribution by outcome, median/IQR dot plots |
| 4 · Profile breakdown | Stacked PA/Life rate bars for 8 attributes, buyer profile table |
| 5 · Propensity model | ROC-AUC, cumulative gains curve, decile lift, permutation importance, contact tiers |
| Data | Field-level dataset summary, 9 data-quality findings |

All charts have hover tooltips, keyboard focus, and a "Show table" view. Everything except the model and the data sections follows the segment filter. The dashboard supports light and dark mode and prints on A4.

## Method notes
- **Analysis set:** the 1,500 rows with no customer profile are excluded (0.07% acceptance, so most likely unmatched records).
- **Dropped columns:** the 15-day flow fields (exact copies of the 30-day fields), `currentacc_bal` and `avg_currentaccbal_30d` (always zero).
- **Model:** `HistGradientBoostingClassifier` with native categorical support. Target = accepted any offer. Stratified 70/30 split. It is evaluated with ROC-AUC, PR-AUC and cumulative gains because the classes are imbalanced (1.2% positive). Feature importance is permutation importance on the hold-out set.
- **Result:** ROC-AUC ≈ 0.72. Contacting the top 20% of customers by score reaches about 49% of buyers, and the top decile converts at about 3× the average.
